log.prompt:
把「Materials and Methods」部分里所有的 “patients” 改成 “participants”，其他章节不要动。

下面是这一部分的全文。只输出修改后的全文，保持段落数量和顺序不变，段落之间空一行，不要解释。

---
This single-arm, multicenter, prospective phase II clinical study was conducted at 4 medical centers across China. The clinical trial was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov under the identifier NCT05348668. Eligible patients (18 to 75 years) had histologically confirmed stage IV driver-negative NSCLC (8th edition of the Tumor–Node–Metastasis [TNM] Staging System 24), Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status 0 to 1, and adequate organ/bone marrow function. Exclusion criteria included driver mutations (e.g., epidermal growth factor receptor [EGFR], anaplastic lymphoma kinase [ALK], and ROS proto-oncogene 1 [ROS1]), pulmonary fibrosis, autoimmune disease, active infection, or serious comorbidities. All patients received 4 to 6 cycles of platinum-based doublet chemotherapy plus ICI. Patients without disease progression after comprehensive evaluation subsequently underwent Hybrid-RT during ICI maintenance. The comprehensive clinical trial protocol is provided in Data S1. This study was reported in accordance with the STROBE statement.

Eligibility to participate in the study required histologically confirmed diagnosis and completion of molecular profiling (including at least EGFR, ALK, ROS1, and programmed cell death ligand 1 [PD-L1] status). All patients were pre-evaluated and staged via bronchoscopy, computed tomography (CT) with contrast, contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the brain, and single-photon emission CT bone scan; positron emission tomography (PET)/CT or PET/MRI was optional. Histopathological diagnosis of suspicious lymph nodes was established via either thoracoscopic biopsy or endosonography-guided needle aspiration as clinically warranted.

All enrolled patients received 4 to 6 cycles of standard platinum-based doublet chemotherapy combined with ICI therapy. Specific chemotherapy regimens and ICI agents were selected at the investigators’ discretion in accordance with both the National Comprehensive Cancer Network guidelines 25 and the Chinese Society of Clinical Oncology guidelines. ICI maintenance continued for up to 24 months or until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, or study withdrawal occurred.

Patients without progression after chemoimmunotherapy received Hybrid-RT during ICI maintenance, completed within 3 months. SABR-eligible lesions were treated with hypofractionated radiotherapy (24 Gy/3 fractions or 50 Gy/4 to 5 fractions), while non-SABR lesions received LDRT (6 to 15 Gy at 1.5 Gy/fraction). For patients who were restaged as stage III disease after chemoimmunotherapy, the primary tumor and regional metastatic lymph nodes received short-course hypofractionated radiotherapy with 48 Gy in 12 fractions, which achieves a biologically effective dose (BED) equivalent to conventional fractionation of 54 Gy in 27 fractions (assuming an α/β ratio of 10 Gy for NSCLC). Target selection and dose schedules are detailed in Tables S1 and S2. The simulation utilized customized vacuum immobilization with intravenous contrast-enhanced 4-dimensional CT. The internal target volume (ITV) was contoured on maximum intensity projection reconstructions, with the planning target volume defined as the ITV plus a 5-mm isotropic margin. All treatments followed predefined plans, minimizing inter-/intra-fractional errors.

The primary endpoint was the 1-year progression-free survival (PFS) rate. PFS was defined as the time from initiation of first-line chemoimmunotherapy to disease progression per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST v1.1) or death from any cause, whichever occurred first. Patients without documented disease progression or death at the time of data cutoff were censored at the date of their last disease assessment. The secondary endpoints were median PFS, 1.5-year and 2-year PFS rates, median overall survival (OS), 1-year and 2-year OS rates, objective response rate (ORR), disease control rate (DCR), and adverse events (AEs). OS was defined as the time from initiation of first-line chemoimmunotherapy to death from any cause (living patients were censored at last follow-up). Per RECIST v1.1, ORR and DCR represented patients achieving complete or partial response, and complete/partial response or stable disease, respectively. Hybrid-RT was initiated no less than 2 weeks after the completion of initial chemoimmunotherapy. Exploratory outcomes included changes in peripheral blood lymphocyte subsets pre-radiotherapy and 3 weeks post-radiotherapy. AEs and laboratory/radiological assessments were performed weekly during chemoimmunotherapy and radiotherapy, and every 3 weeks during ICI maintenance. AEs were graded according to the Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE version 4.0). Tumor assessments per RECIST v1.1 were conducted every 9 weeks in the first year, every 3 months in the second year, and every 6 months thereafter.

Peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) obtained from 40 patients who received Hybrid-RT (SABR + LDRT) at the First Affiliated Hospital of University of Science and Technology of China (USTC) were isolated within 2 h of EDTA anticoagulated blood collection using Ficoll-Paque (Cat. #17144002, Cytiva) density gradient centrifugation. All patients completed chemoimmunotherapy ≥2 weeks prior to Hybrid-RT. Peripheral blood was collected immediately before radiotherapy and 3 weeks after treatment completion. Immune cells were analyzed via clinical-grade flow cytometry and were defined as follows: CD3+ T cells (CD45+CD3+), T helper cells (Th; CD45+CD3+CD4+CD8−), granzyme B (GZMB)+ Th cells (CD45+CD3+CD4+CD8−GZMB+), CD8+ T cells (CD45+CD3+CD8+CD4−), cytotoxic CD8+ T cells (cyto-CD8+ T; CD45+CD3+CD8+CD4−GZMB+), natural killer cells (NK; CD45+CD3−CD56dim), and cytotoxic NK cells (cyto-NK; CD45+CD3−CD56dimGZMB+).

C57BL/6 mice (5 weeks old, male) were obtained from Shanghai SLAC Laboratory Animal Co., Ltd. and housed in a specific pathogen-free barrier facility at the Core Facility Center of the First Affiliated Hospital of USTC. Murine Lewis lung carcinoma (LLC) cells (Cat. #QuiCell-L214, QuiCell Biotechnology Co., Ltd.) were cultured in Dulbecco’s modified Eagle medium (DMEM) supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS) at 37 °C with 5% CO₂. DMEM (Cat. #10566016, Gibco) and FBS (Cat. #A5669701, Gibco) were purchased from Ketu Biotech Co., Ltd. Mycoplasma contamination was routinely monitored every 2 weeks. Subcutaneous tumors (primary lesions) were established by injecting 2.5 × 105 LLC cells into the right flank on day –21, and lung metastases were induced on the same day by intravenous injection of 5 × 105 LLC cells via the tail vein (experimental metastasis model). From day –21 to day 0, tumors were allowed to grow without intervention.

SABR was delivered on days 1, 3, and 5; LDRT was delivered on days 7, 12, and 17. Anti-programmed death receptor 1 (anti-PD-1; Cat. #BE0146, BioXCell), anti-C-X-C motif chemokine receptor 3 (anti-Cxcr3; Cat. #BE0249, BioXCell), and anti-natural killer group 2 member D (anti-NKG2D; Cat. #BE0111, BioXCell) were administered intraperitoneally at 200 μg per mouse on days 7, 12, and 17. For irradiation, tumor-bearing mice were anesthetized with isoflurane (induction 2%, maintenance 1.5%; Cat. #HY-A0134, MedChemExpress), and the irradiation sites were fully exposed. Targeted pulmonary or subcutaneous tumors were irradiated using a rodent-specific x-ray irradiator (Cat. #SHARP 100, Raycision Medical Technology Co., Ltd.). For lung metastatic lesions, a dose of 1 Gy (1 Gy/min, 225 kV) was delivered to the entire lung, while subcutaneous tumors (primary lesions) received 8 Gy (1 Gy/min, 225 kV). Serial micro-CT imaging was performed using a micro-CT scanner (Cat. #IMAGING 100, Raycision Medical Technology Co., Ltd.) on days 0, 7, and 21. Tumor volume (V) was calculated as V = (length × width2)/2, where length was the longest diameter and width was the perpendicular diameter. Mice were euthanized on day 21, and tumors, lung tissues, and serum were collected for analysis.

Tissue samples were fixed in 4% paraformaldehyde (Cat. #BL539A, Biosharp) for 24 h, paraffin-embedded, and sectioned at 4 μm thickness. For hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining, sections were deparaffinized, rehydrated, and stained according to standard protocols. For Masson’s staining, sections were stained with a Masson’s trichrome stain kit (Cat. #C0189S, Beyotime) according to the manufacturer’s instructions. For immunohistochemistry (IHC), antigen retrieval was performed using citrate buffer (pH 6.0; Cat. #BL604A, Biosharp) at 95 °C for 15 min, followed by blocking of endogenous peroxidase activity with 3% hydrogen peroxide (Cat. #abs9333, Absin). Sections were incubated overnight at 4 °C with primary antibodies against NK1.1 (Cat. #ab289542, Abcam), transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-β; Cat. #21898-1-AP, Proteintech), followed by incubation with secondary antibodies at 37 °C for 1 h, and visualized using a 3,3′-diaminobenzidine substrate kit (Cat. #ab64238, Abcam). The antibodies used for IHC staining are listed in Table S3. After hematoxylin counterstaining, staining intensity and distribution were quantified using Fiji software (ImageJ v1.53t, https://fiji.sc/) based on standardized thresholds.

Tissues were prepared as described for IHC. Sections were incubated overnight at 4 °C with primary antibodies against CD8 (Cat. #ab217344, Abcam), CD3 (Cat. #ab135372, Abcam), NK1.1 (Cat. #ab289542, Abcam), CXCR3 (Cat. #ab288437, Abcam), C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 10 (CXCL10, Cat. #10937-1-AP, Proteintech), GZMB (Cat. #13588-1-AP, Proteintech), F4/80 (Cat. #sc-52664, Santa Cruz), and secreted phosphoprotein 1 (SPP1, Cat. #sc-21742, Santa Cruz). After washing, sections were incubated at room temperature for 1 h with Cy3 Goat-Anti-Rabbit IgG (H + L) (Cat. #ab6939, Abcam), Alexa Fluor 488 Goat-Anti-Mouse IgG (H + L) (Cat. #ab150113, Abcam), and Cy5 Goat-Anti-Rabbit IgG (H + L) (Cat. #ab6564, Abcam). The antibodies used for multiplex immunofluorescence (mIF) staining are listed in Table S3. Sections were mounted with 4′,6-diamidino-2-phenylindole (DAPI) containing anti-fade mounting medium (Cat. #F6057, Sigma) and examined by fluorescence microscopy.

Single-cell suspensions were prepared from lung/tumor tissues by mechanical dissociation and filtration through a 70-μm filter. The cells were washed in cold phosphate-buffered saline (PBS, Cat. #BL302A, Biosharp), resuspended at 1 × 107 cells/ml, and Fc-blocked (Cat. #15660, BioLegend) prior to surface staining. To explore intracellular targets, cells were fixed/permeabilized with BD Cytofix/Cytoperm (Cat. #554714, BD Biosciences) and then stained with antibodies against cytokines/activation markers. The samples were analyzed on a BD FACSCelesta using FlowJo (v10.9, https://www.flowjo.com/docs/flowjo10). Details regarding the antibodies used are provided in Table S3.

All tissue samples were collected on day 21. Fresh tissue samples (n = 3/group) were dissociated into single-cell suspensions using the GentleMACS Dissociator (Cat. #130-093-235, Miltenyi Biotec) and filtered through 30-μm strainers. Cell viability (>85%) was confirmed via Trypan blue (Cat. #T8154, Sigma-Aldrich) exclusion. The fixed cells were hybridized with species-specific probes using the Chromium X system (10x Genomics, Pleasanton). The obtained libraries were sequenced on the NovaSeq 6000 platform (Illumina; 150 bp paired-end, ≥20,000 reads/cell). The data were processed with Cell Ranger (v7.1.0, https://support.10xgenomics.com/) and analyzed using Seurat (v4.3, https://satijalab.org/seurat/), excluding low-quality cells (<500 genes/cell, >15% mitochondrial reads). Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) was performed using clusterProfiler (v4.6.0) in R (v4.3.1, https://www.r-project.org/) against MSigDB (https://www.gsea-msigdb.org/gsea/msigdb) hallmark gene sets; pathways with false discovery rate (FDR) < 0.25 were considered significant. The scRNA-seq analysis was performed by OE Biotech (Shanghai, China).

Cell–cell communication networks were inferred using CellChat (v2.1.2) in R (v4.3.1, https://www.r-project.org/). The normalized expression matrix was imported and used to generate a CellChat object, followed by preprocessing to identify overexpressed genes and ligand–receptor interactions using default parameters. Communication probabilities were calculated (computeCommunProb) and filtered to exclude interactions with fewer than 10 cells (filterCommunication), and pathway-level networks were aggregated (aggregateNet). Signaling pathways were prioritized on the basis of interaction strength and network centrality.

Serum levels of cytokines were quantified using the Luminex X-200 system (Luminex) according to the manufacturer’s instructions (LX-MultiDTH-10, LabEx Co.).

Clinical efficacy analyses followed the intention-to-treat (ITT) principle. Based on historical control data 26–28, a sample size of 74 patients (including an estimated 10% dropout rate) was calculated to provide 80% power to detect an improvement in the 1-year PFS rate from 35% to 50%, using a one-sided α level of 0.05. The cutoff date was 2025 September 30. For the clinical trial, survival outcomes were measured from first-line chemoimmunotherapy initiation. The comprehensive clinical statistical analysis plan is provided in the Data S2. SPP1+ macrophage-associated signature scores were calculated using bulk RNA-sequencing data from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) and lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC) cohorts (https://www.cancer.gov/tcga). Single-sample gene set enrichment analysis (ssGSEA) was performed using a marker gene set derived from the GSE127465 single-cell RNA-sequencing dataset. These scores reflect transcriptional enrichment. The optimal cutoff for the SPP1+ macrophage-associated signature score was determined using the survminer R package (v0.5.1). Patients were classified into high-score (≥ cutoff) and low-score (< cutoff) groups. All experiments were independently replicated 3 times with consistent results, and representative data are shown. The statistical tests used for data analysis included Student’s t test, one-way repeated-measures analysis of variance (ANOVA), the χ2 test, and the log-rank test; differential gene expression was assessed using the Wilcoxon rank-sum test with Benjamini–Hochberg correction. Survival curves were estimated using the Kaplan–Meier method and compared using the log-rank test. The data were analyzed using SPSS (v25.0, https://www.ibm.com/docs/spss-statistics) and R (v4.3.1, https://www.r-project.org/). Statistical significance was defined as P < 0.05.

At the cutoff date (2025 September 30), the median follow-up for all patients was 24.3 months (interquartile range 6.6 to 44.4 months). In our study, the 1-year PFS rate was 54.2%, exceeding the prespecified target. The 1.5-year and 2-year PFS rates were 42.2% and 28.6%, respectively, with a median PFS of 16.1 months (95% CI 11.4 to 19.2 months; Fig. 1G). The 1-year and 2-year OS rates were 83.1% and 57.7%, respectively, and the median OS was 29.3 months (95% CI 21.9 months to not reached; Fig. 1H). The ORR and DCR were 69.9% (58/83; 95% CI 58.8% to 79.5%) and 91.6% (76/83; 95% CI 83.4% to 96.5%), respectively (Fig. 2A and B). A total of 14 patients (16.9%) were downstaged to stage III and received hypofractionated radiotherapy. Among the remaining 69 patients, median PFS was 16.8 months (95% CI 11.3 to 19.2 months), and median OS was 24.0 months (95% CI 21.2 to 25.4 months). No statistically significant differences in PFS (P = 0.57; Fig. S1A) or OS (P = 0.45; Fig. S1B) were observed between the 14 patients who were downstaged to stage III and the remaining 69 patients. A total of 32 patients (38.6%) had distant metastasis beyond radiotherapy lesions, and 9 patients (10.8%) experienced both radiotherapy lesion progression and distant metastasis. Background: Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-based chemoimmunotherapy has become a standard first-line treatment for patients with driver-negative metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but the clinical benefit is limited. Radiotherapy has potential antitumor immunomodulatory effects, but the optimal dose and fractionation remain unclear. Methods: This single-arm, multicenter, prospective, phase II trial enrolled patients with stage IV driver-negative NSCLC who received first-line chemoimmunotherapy. During the ICI maintenance phase, patients received hybrid dose-fraction radiotherapy (Hybrid-RT): stereotactic ablative body radiotherapy (SABR) to targetable lesions and low-dose radiotherapy (LDRT) to other sites. Patients restaged to stage III disease after chemoimmunotherapy received short-course hypofractionated radiotherapy to all residual lesions. The primary endpoint was 1-year progression-free survival (PFS) rate. The secondary endpoints included 1-year overall survival (OS) rate, objective response rate, and safety. Parallel preclinical mechanistic studies were performed in a murine model. Results: A total of 83 patients were enrolled from 2022 May 9 to 2023 December 31. The 1-year PFS rate was 54.2% (median PFS 16.1 months; 95% confidence interval [CI] 11.4 to 19.2 months), meeting the primary endpoint. The 1-year OS rate was 83.1% (median OS 29.3 months; 95% CI 21.9 months to not reached), and treatment was well tolerated. Peripheral immune profiling showed posttreatment expansion of cytotoxic CD8+ T cells and natural killer (NK) cells associated with promising clinical efficacy. In the murine model, ICI plus Hybrid-RT (IHBRT) induced a division of labor between CD8+ T and NK cells. At LDRT lesions, it facilitated both C-X-C motif chemokine receptor 3 (Cxcr3)-mediated recruitment of cytotoxic CD8+ T cells and natural killer group 2 member D-mediated NK cell cytotoxicity. At SABR lesions, Cxcr3-mediated CD8+ T cells played a predominant role, whereas NK cells contributed minimally. Moreover, IHBRT suppressed secreted phosphoprotein 1 positive (Spp1+) macrophages and relieved immunosuppression. Conclusions: Clinically, IHBRT demonstrates promising efficacy and a manageable safety profile in driver-negative metastatic NSCLC. Preclinically, it induces a functional division of labor between CD8+ T and NK cells to activate antitumor immune cytotoxicity, and suppresses Spp1+ macrophages, thereby relieving immunosuppression. Trial registration: This trial was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (Identifier: NCT05348668). Date of registration: 2022 April 26.

Given the complementary immunomodulatory effects of SABR and LDRT, the triple combination of SABR + LDRT + ICI is biologically rational 21, 51, 52. A phase Ib study evaluated a chemotherapy-free regimen that combines SABR, LDRT, and sintilimab for the treatment of PD-L1-positive stage IV NSCLC and revealed acceptable safety and evidence of LDRT-induced immune modulation 23. However, its median PFS of 8.6 months did not exceed historical benchmarks for standard ICI or chemoimmunotherapy 53, 54. By contrast, our study used standard first-line chemoimmunotherapy regardless of PD-L1 status. Although PD-L1-high tumors may derive greater benefit from single-agent ICI, chemotherapy-free strategies remain restricted to patients with PD-L1 ≥50% 55, 56. Importantly, our results revealed no significant PFS or OS advantage in PD-L1-high patients compared with PD-L1-low/negative patients. IHBRT triggers broad immune activation and reshapes the tumor immune landscape, with efficacy observed across PD-L1 subgroups. This is consistent with trials suggesting radiotherapy may benefit PD-L1-negative/low NSCLC 10, 57, 58, supporting its potential broader applicability. We acknowledge that the lack of posttreatment biopsies prevents us from evaluating dynamic PD-L1 alterations during treatment. Additionally, no significant difference in PFS and OS was observed between squamous and nonsquamous subgroups in this study, despite prior reports suggesting squamous NSCLC may have inferior chemoimmunotherapy responses 27, 59–61. Thus, IHBRT demonstrates broad applicability irrespective of PD-L1 expression and histologic subtype.
